title: The Grand Ole Opry Cast
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the Grand Ole Opry, the longest-running live radio broadcast in US history, based in Nashville, Tennessee. They cover its origins as the WSM "Barn Dance" on the fifth floor of the National Life and Accident Insurance Company building, its venue moves (Hillsborough Theater, Dixie Tabernacle, War Memorial Auditorium, the Ryman, and the Grand Ole Opry House in 1974), membership rules and famous members, banishments and controversies (Hank Williams, Johnny Cash, Skeeter Davis, Nicole Case, Jerry Lee Lewis, the Byrds), the rise of rock and roll and drums, Opryland USA amusement park and its closure, and a listener mail correction about Chinatown pronunciation. Chuck also mentions his WSM radio playlist hour airing July 1.
topics: rock and roll and country music

entities.name: National Life and Accident Insurance Company

segments.title: Opening banter and WSM playlist hour
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Chuck's guest DJ hour on WSM Radio's WSM Playlist, airing July 1 at 5 pm Central, and set up the episode on the Grand Ole Opry.

segments.title: Origins as the WSM Barn Dance
segments.summary: The show began as a radio broadcast from the fifth floor of the National Life and Accident Insurance Company building in Nashville, starting from the National Barn Dance in Chicago. George D. Hay renamed it the Grand Ole Opry, and the WSM call letters are explained.

segments.title: Nashville's image and the move through venues
segments.summary: Nashville's leaders resented the Opry's rural image. The show moved from the insurance building to the Hillsborough Theater, the Dixie Tabernacle, and War Memorial Auditorium, where tickets were sold, then to the Ryman Theater in 1943, and was broadcast nationally on NBC in 1939.

segments.title: Early stars and Opry membership
segments.summary: Early stars such as Roy Acuff and Minnie Pearl are discussed, including the character behind Minnie Pearl. The hosts explain how Opry cast membership works, its requirements of twelve shows a year, and past members such as Bill Monroe, Hank Williams, Johnny Cash, and Reba.

segments.title: Rock and roll, drums, and famous expulsions
segments.summary: The Opry's resistance to drums, horns, and electric guitars is covered along with Jerry Lee Lewis's 1993 appearance. Hank Williams was expelled in 1952, Johnny Cash was removed in 1965 and later reinstated, and Skeeter Davis lost her membership for speaking out about arrests of church workers.

segments.title: Nicole Case ban and the move to Opry House
segments.summary: Nicole Case was banned for life after removing her shirt during a hot outdoor performance. The Opry moved from the Ryman to the Grand Ole Opry House in 1974, and the Ryman later faced demolition threats before being saved.

segments.title: Opryland USA and closure
segments.summary: Opryland USA, the theme park near the Opry House, is discussed, including its closure and replacement by a mall in 1997, the 2010 Cumberland River flood, and Dollywood's rise. Chuck recalls visiting as a child.

segments.title: Listener mail: Chinatown pronunciation
segments.summary: A listener named Sean corrects the pronunciation of Canton's Chinatown name, saying Josh pronounced it correctly. He also says he listens to the show on Google Home.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and direct listeners to the show's contact address.
